text:
amal: Heads-up — we're planning to enable stricter ptls enforcement in EU + APAC next maintenance window. This could break unwrap for any rotators still running legacy SAs. Any immediate blockers?

kevin: noted. my narrow-kms-principals change is already staged; rotator job identity rotation might be incomplete in some clusters.

sam: saw a couple DecryptAccessDenied in apac-staging yesterday: `kms:DecryptAccessDenied principal=svc-rotator-old@apac-staging key=projects/redwood/locations/apac/keys/keystore-main`

marie: if rotator can't unwrap, edge won't receive client certs -> mutual auth failures. we had a ~2.7% uplift in 403s on /internal/auth during a test window.

incident-bot: alert: unwrap error spike correlated to rotator failures (apac-staging) 2026-04-02T03:14Z-03:18Z

amal: OK. two quick mitigations: (A) apply conditional, short-lived KMS decrypt binding for legacy rotator SAs, or (B) roll back the principal-narrowing PR. A is lower blast radius.

kevin: I can apply a conditional IAM grant with `condition: request.time < timestamp("2026-04-09T00:00:00Z")` and file ticket SEC-1023. will annotate change for audit and set a reminder to remove.

sam: while we do that, please add a ROTATOR_REQ_ID env var and surface it in unwrap logs so KMS audit entries can be correlated to job runs (req_id -> kms_request_id).

dylan: also recommend adding `service_identity_v` to keystore logs so we can detect partial rollouts. include the SA email and a rotation tag.

kevin: applied binding at 2026-04-02T03:20Z, ticket=SEC-1023, expiry=2026-04-09T00:00:00Z. change present in audit: projects/redwood/locations/apac/keys/keystore-main policy update.

ops-oncall: incident-bot: unwrap failures dropped to baseline after change. ptls-client-cert-missing alert cleared.

amal: action items: kevin=temporary KMS binding + ticket; sam=instrument ROTATOR_REQ_ID + demo in staging (ETA EOD); dylan=RBAC rollout playbook draft (ETA 48h); marie=add ptls-client-cert-missing canary alert (ETA EOD). We'll only schedule full ptls enforcement after playbook review. :thumbsup:
